unattestable.claim: verify PASS, which grant:standing-landing-loop requires as landing evidence
unattestable.method: three interleaved rounds per side, measured by me, on a box carrying 19 python processes and 58 worktrees
unattestable.finding: UNATTESTABLE ON THIS MACHINE TONIGHT, AND NOT THIS COMMIT'S FAULT. main 23.692s, 21.942s, 22.358s; landing 22.697s, 23.821s, 26.406s; ceiling 15.000s. Both sides fail. Four things settle the attribution. Main carries none of this change and fails on its own. I measured these same two worktrees earlier this session at 14.180s and 13.630s for main and 13.741s and 13.785s for a sibling commit, all PASS - same commits, opposite verdict, hours apart. The two checks this change registers cost 0.095s combined, which cannot account for a 7 to 9 second move. And the ordering is unstable: the builder measured landing faster in two of three rounds and I measured it slower in two of three, on a spread that swamps the signal. The honest statement is that the budget is not measurable here tonight, in either direction. I record it as an unmet precondition rather than as a defect, and I decline to present any single favourable run as the reading - which is also what the builder declined to do, correctly.
unattestable.what_would_settle_it: one interleaved pair on a quiet box, or decisions/0081 landing and changing what the budget means. Neither is mine and neither is the builder's.

residuals.finding: The stated rule is one-directional and two in-set characters also cause a miss. The comment says a key body is the ASCII letter, digit, underscore, dot, hyphen and slash set, and that is exactly right about the body: the pattern is a leading letter-or-digit followed by that class. Because the leading character is narrower than the body, a leading dot and a leading slash are both in the stated set and both make a valid YAML status key invisible. The shape worth naming is the second one: the comment lists path-like among the forms the reader TAKES, and services/asset_status is indeed taken, while /services/asset_status is invisible. An absolute path key differs from a relative one by a single character and the two land on opposite sides. I grade this MINOR and explicitly not a landing objection, and I want the difference from K4-B1 on the record rather than left to inference: that finding was an enumeration naming 7 of 29 characters in one position and missing an entire category; this is a true rule that does not extend to one character position. It is an order of magnitude smaller, it carries the same zero behavioural risk, and I do not think it justifies another cycle on its own. If the builder is editing this file for another reason, the closing words are that the key must also start with a letter or digit. If not, leaving it is a defensible call and I would not withhold for it.

preconditions_the_grant_requires.verify_PASS: NOT EVIDENCED. Both sides fail the verification budget on this machine tonight, main included. This is a property of the box, not of the change, and it cannot be resolved by re-running until a favourable number appears.

landing_assessment.my_view: I am not withholding on the residual and I want that unambiguous. The content is done, and I would confirm it on its own. What is missing is a precondition the grant names and that neither the builder nor I can produce tonight: verify PASS, on a machine where main itself takes 22 seconds against a 15 second ceiling. The builder was right to refuse to present a favourable run as the reading, and right that this is decisions/0081's argument rather than a question about this change. So: land it when an interleaved pair on a quiet box shows both sides green, or when 0081 settles what the budget means. Until one of those, the honest position is that the change is ready and the gate is not measurable - and those are two different sentences that should not be collapsed into one verdict.

standing_supported: Supports OPEN to BUILT for the ten paths and supports the content half of BUILT to WITNESSED without reservation. The rule now stated in place of the enumeration is true: I swept every printable ASCII character plus five non-ASCII cases in three key positions, recovering the parsed key before judging visibility, and of 87 lines whose key genuinely carries an out-of-set character 86 are invisible exactly as claimed, with the single exception erring safe by refusing rather than missing. Every non-ASCII letter is covered, which no list had reached. The three retained factual claims are each re-measured and true. The pattern itself is byte-identical across all four commits of this sequence, so three rounds of re-description have changed no behaviour, and the full battery confirms that independently. The prose sweep finds no eighth site and every surviving count checks out. It does not support BUILT to WITNESSED as a completed landing, and the reason is not a defect in the change: verify PASS is a precondition the landing grant names, and tonight it fails on main as well as on the commit, on a box carrying 19 python processes where I measured these same worktrees passing at under 14 seconds hours earlier. That is unattestable rather than failed, and stating it as a precondition rather than folding it into the content grade is the distinction this observation is written to preserve. The one content residual - that a leading dot or slash is in the stated body class and still makes a key invisible, so an absolute path key is missed where a relative one is refused - is recorded as MINOR, explicitly non-blocking, and an order of magnitude smaller than the finding it descends from.

judgement_items.question: The verification budget now fails on main itself on this machine, at 22 seconds against a 15 second ceiling, while the same commit passed at under 14 seconds earlier the same evening. Whether the gate passes therefore depends on when it runs. Does the landing grant's verify PASS requirement mean PASS on the machine at the moment of landing, or PASS on a quiet machine, and should a budget failure that reproduces identically on the base be admissible as evidence against a change at all?

Unchanged: contracts/status-claims.json names decisions/0074 as its governing decision and that record cannot land with the code because decisions/ is outside grant:standing-landing-loop. Should verify grade a contract's decision and governed_by paths for existence, forcing a contract to land with its decision, or is a contract permitted to name its governing decision before the record exists?

Four readings have each found prose claiming slightly more than the code supports, and each repair was correct, smaller than the last, and reachable by the next reader. The durable move each time was to state the rule that produces the behaviour rather than the examples a witness brought. Is that worth recording as a lesson - a claim about an artifact should be written against the rule that generates it, never against a sample - or has the sequence itself made the point well enough to leave in the record and stop?
